born May 20, 1995) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] and [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] He was selected with the 31st overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the Bucks and represents [[France national basketball team|France]] in international competition. ==Early life== Born in [[Cayenne]], [[French Guiana]], Inglis was a big soccer fan, but as his cousins played [[streetball]], he first began playing basketball at age nine before moving to [[Paris]] as a teenager.{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Charles|title=Bad breaks won't derail Damien Inglis' NBA dream|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/bucks/bad-breaks-wont-derail-damien-inglis-nba-dream-b99328445z1-270830761.html|website=JSOnline.com|date=11 August 2014|access-date=26 December 2014}} Several years later, he recalled his move to Paris saying, "I was by myself. I left French Guiana when I was 14 years old. My family was far and I had to play basketball. It was cold, it was tough. I was family-sick, homesick. But I really wanted to make it, so that’s why I kept going."{{cite web|last1=Chouinard|first1=KL|title=Damien Inglis: "I'm moving to Milwaukee right after the Summer League"|url=http://www.bucksketball.com/2014/07/damien-inglis-im-moving-to-milwaukee-right-after-the-summer-league/|website=Bucksetball.com|access-date=29 July 2014}} Inglis grew up playing with [[INSEP]], a French training institute for excellence in sports. The school had been previously attended by several promising [[NBA]] players such as [[Tony Parker]], [[Boris Diaw]] and [[Ronny Turiaf]]. During his time with INSEP, he participated in two [[Euroleague Basketball Nike International Junior Tournament|Nike International Junior Tournaments]]. ==Professional career== ===Centre Fédéral (2010–2013)=== In association with INSEP, Inglis played for [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball]] of the [[Nationale Masculine 1]], the third level professional league in France, from 2010 to 2013. While mostly playing for the U21 team in 2010–11, he did manage two games for Centre Fédéral, averaging three points and three rebounds per game. In 2011–12, he played 28 games, averaging 5.9 points and 3.4 rebounds per game. On October 6, 2012, Inglis recorded 16 points, 11 rebounds and 6 assists against Cognac Charente Basketball{{cite web|title=Centre Federal Du Basket-Ball 57, Cognac BB 71|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-10-06/Centre-Federal-Du-Basket-Ball-at-Cognac-BB/131232|website=RealGM.com|access-date=28 July 2014}} and scored a season-high 31 points on November 10, 2012, against ADA Blois Basket, also adding on with nine total rebounds. The team would still lose the game by over 20 points.{{cite web|title=Centre Federal Du Basket-Ball 81, ADA Blois Basket 102|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-11-10/Centre-Federal-Du-Basket-Ball-at-ADA-Blois-Basket/131274|website=RealGM.com|access-date=28 July 2014}} In 2012–13, he averaged 15.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.2 blocks per game. {{multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | width = | image1 = Damien Inglis (2).jpg | width1 = 130 | caption1 = | image2 = Kevin Seraphin Wizards.jpg | width2 = 200 | caption2 = | header_align = | header_background = | footer = After signing with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Inglis (left) became the second active French Guianese player in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], the other one being [[Kevin Séraphin]] (right).{{cite web|last1=Chouinard|first1=KL|title=Damien Inglis: "I'm moving to Milwaukee right after the Summer League"|url=http://www.bucksketball.com/2014/07/damien-inglis-im-moving-to-milwaukee-right-after-the-summer-league/|work=Bucksetball.com|date=July 10, 2014|access-date=July 29, 2014}} | footer_align = | footer_background = }} Inglis returned to NIJT play on February 22, 2013, against the [[KK Cedevita]] junior team, with 17 points, 8 rebounds, and 8 assists.{{cite web|title=KK Cedevita Junior Team 50, INSEP 88|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-02-22/KK-Cedevita-Junior-Team-at-INSEP/120293|website=RealGM.com|access-date=28 July 2014}} Inglis scored 30 points against the USK Future Stars, marking his career-high scoring record in the event.{{cite web|title=INSEP 86, USK Future Stars 75|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-02-22/INSEP-at-USK-Future-Stars/120298|website=RealGM.com|access-date=28 July 2014}} Due to his success through the competition, Inglis was named to the 2013 NIKE International Junior All-Tournament team. Other recipients of the award were [[Nikola Jokić]], Vasilije Pusica, [[Nikola Rebić]], and [[Dušan Ristić]].{{cite web|title=Belgrade Tournament (NIJT) Awards|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/46/Belgrade-Tournament-NIJT/awards/by_season/2013|website=RealGM.com|access-date=28 July 2014}} ===Chorale Roanne (2013–2014)=== On June 4, 2013, Inglis signed a three-year deal with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web|title=Chorale Roanne signs prospect Damien Inglis|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/101683/chorale-roanne-signs-prospect-damien-inglis.html|work=Sportando.com|date=June 4, 2013|access-date=July 9, 2014}} He debuted with the team on October 5, 2013, with 5 points and 2 rebounds against [[BCM Gravelines]]. Inglis also shot 2-of-3 from the field and made his only three-pointer attempted.{{cite web|title=Chorale Roanne Basket 64, BCM Gravelines 65|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-10-05/Chorale-Roanne-Basket-at-BCM-Gravelines/132200|website=RealGM.com|access-date=29 July 2014}} His first double-digit scoring performance took place on November 2, 2013, when he logged 14 points, 7 rebounds, and 1 assist against [[JDA Dijon Basket]].{{cite web|title=JDA Dijon Basket 60, Chorale Roanne Basket 69|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-11-02/JDA-Dijon-Basket-at-Chorale-Roanne-Basket/133012|website=RealGM.com|access-date=29 July 2014}} Inglis was finally allowed a start by head coach Luka Pavičević on December 14, 2013, against [[Orléans Loiret Basket]], recording 3 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 assists.{{cite web|title=Chorale Roanne Basket 77, Orleans Loiret Basket 80|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-12-14/Chorale-Roanne-Basket-at-Orleans-Loiret-Basket/133077|website=RealGM.com|access-date=29 July 2014}} In 2013–14, he played 27 games, averaging 4.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game. Following the season, Inglis commented on the experience of playing basketball in France, "My first year on a professional team was great. Even though my team dropped down to the second league, I had a good year. I played against good players. It was a great experience for me." ===Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2016)=== On June 26, 2014, Inglis was selected with the 31st overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|last=Rothstein|first=Ethan|title=The Bucks select Damien Inglis With 31st pick in 2014 NBA Draft|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848076/nba-draft-results-2014-bucks-damien-inglis|work=SBNation.com|date=June 26, 2013|access-date=July 9, 2014}}{{cite web|last1=Magiera|first1=Lauren|title=Bucks take F Damien Inglis in 2nd round|url=http://www.waow.com/story/25884631/2014/06/27/bucks-take-f-damien-inglis-in-2nd-round|work=WAOW.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714161320/http://www.waow.com/story/25884631/2014/06/27/bucks-take-f-damien-inglis-in-2nd-round|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}} Due to a broken foot he suffered during a pre-draft workout with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], he sat out the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|last1=Gardner|first1=Chris|title=Broken foot to sideline Bucks' Inglis during summer|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/264900531.html|work=jsonline.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}} After the event, Inglis said that Milwaukee would become "one of the destinations" for [[French Guiana|French Guianese]] immigrants in the United States. He was also compared with [[Kevin Séraphin]] after becoming just the second French Guianese player to be selected in the NBA draft. On August 26, 2014, he signed with the Bucks.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16482|title=Bucks sign second-round pick Damien Inglis|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 26, 2014|access-date=July 18, 2015}} Following a [[X-ray computed tomography|CT scan]] performed in mid-October, Inglis was ruled out for a further six weeks after it was revealed his fractured right foot was not healing properly. Inglis said, "I don't know if they messed up my surgery back in June, but something happened. I'm still not healthy."{{cite web|last=Gruman|first=Andrew|title=Bucks Friday: Injured rookie Inglis to miss six more weeks|url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/bucks-injured-rookie-inglis-will-be-out-six-more-weeks-102414|website=FOXSports.com|date=24 October 2014|access-date=26 December 2014}} He was later ruled out for the rest of the 2014–15 season on January 5, 2015, after he underwent successful surgery on his ankle.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/injury-update-damien-inglis|title=INJURY UPDATE ON DAMIEN INGLIS|date=January 5, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 5, 2015}} In July 2015, Inglis joined the Bucks for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 3.8 points and 2.5 rebounds in four games, ending what was a successful first outing for Inglis with the Bucks.{{cite web|url=http://dairylandexpress.com/2015/07/19/bucks-expect-rashad-vaughn-damien-inglis/|title=Bucks: What to expect from Rashad Vaughn, Damien Inglis|date=July 19, 2015|work=DairylandExpress.com|access-date=July 19, 2015}} He made his long-awaited debut for the Bucks in the team's season opener against the New York Knicks on October 28, recording 3 points and 4 rebounds in a 122–97 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 24, Knicks beat Bucks 122-97 in opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026223709/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 26, 2015|url-status=dead}} On web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-assign-damien-inglis-canton-charge|title=BUCKS ASSIGN DAMIEN INGLIS TO CANTON CHARGE|date=November 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 22, 2015}} On the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-assign-damien-inglis-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS ASSIGN DAMIEN INGLIS TO WESTCHESTER KNICKS|date=January 16, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 16, 2016}} On February 29, he was recalled by the Bucks after averaging 9.9 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.4 steals and 21.4 minutes in 13 games for Westchester.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-recall-damien-inglis-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS RECALL DAMIEN INGLIS FROM THE WESTCHESTER KNICKS|date=February 29, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 29, 2016}} On June 29, 2016, he was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Charles F.|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/384903521.html|title=Bucks waive Damien Inglis, Johnny O'Bryant|date=June 29, 2016|work=jsonline.com|access-date=July 2, 2016}} In July 2016, Inglis joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. On October 11, 2016, he signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Damien Inglis|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-damien-inglis|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 12, 2016|date=October 11, 2016}} He was waived by the Knicks ten days later.{{cite web|title=Knicks waive Lou Amundson, Cleanthony Early, Chasson Randle, J.P. In a total of 70 games, Inglis averaged 7.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2 assists per contest. ===Yokohama B-Corsairs (2024–2026)=== On September 1, 2024, Inglis signed with [[Yokohama B-Corsairs]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web |title=Damien Inglis moving to Japan for next season |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1711469/damien-inglis-moving-to-japan-for-next-season/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=1 September 2024 |language=en |date=1 September 2024}} ===Bahçeşehir Koleji (2026–present)=== On July 1, 2026, he signed with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BKBasketbol |number=2082058778938400788 |title=Damien Inglis Bahçeşehir Koleji’nde!}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2015}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2015–16 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 20 || 1 || 7.8 || .351 || .231 || .875 || 1.6 || .5 || .3 || .2 || 1.8 |- |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan=2| Career | 20 || 1 || 7.8 || .351 || .231 || .875 || 1.6 || .5 || .3 || .2 || 1.8 {{S-end}} ===EuroLeague=== {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2023–24]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] | 32 || 23 || 20.5 || .507 || .280 || .710 || 4.7 || 1.7 || .7 || .2 || 8.2 || 9.6 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan=2| Career | 32 || 23 || 20.5 || .507 || .280 || .710 || 4.7 || 1.7 || .7 || .2 || 8.2 || 9.6 {{S-end}} ==National team career== Inglis first played for the [[France national basketball team|France junior national team]] at the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], averaging 4.5 points and 5.0 rebounds in 8 games as his team finished sixth place in the competition.
